title: Reusable Embedded Platforms and Product Variability

standard.family: AutoLeaP Embedded Systems Body of Knowledge

summary: A platform is a governed set of reusable capabilities and contracts with a support commitment. It is not merely a shared repository. Product teams need predictable APIs, compatibility, documentation, integration environments and ownership. Platform teams need clear target products and product feedback. Reuse is valuable when it reduces lead time and risk while preserving product differentiation.
learningObjectives: Separate platform capability from product-specific behavior.
Design variability, extension and compatibility mechanisms.
Create governance that increases reuse without blocking products.
explanation: A platform is a governed set of reusable capabilities and contracts with a support commitment. It is not merely a shared repository. Product teams need predictable APIs, compatibility, documentation, integration environments and ownership. Platform teams need clear target products and product feedback. Reuse is valuable when it reduces lead time and risk while preserving product differentiation.

Commonality should capture stable behavior and infrastructure. Variability should represent legitimate differences in hardware, capability, policy or UX. Configuration selects supported options; extension points allow bounded specialization. Source forks and unscoped conditional compilation usually indicate that variability has not been modeled.

API governance includes source, binary, behavioral, timing and data compatibility. A change that preserves function but alters latency or failure behavior can still break an embedded consumer. Exceptions should be time-bounded, owned and paired with a migration decision. Platform success is measured through product outcomes, adoption, quality and lifecycle cost—not component count.
whyItMatters: Poor platform design either blocks product delivery or creates uncontrolled product forks.
A product-family architecture creates option value for future products, suppliers and hardware changes.
activities: Define APIs, extension points and version policy
Measure adoption, lead time, escapes and migration
outputs: Platform operating metrics and support model
automotiveExample: Three machine families share connectivity, user identity and update services. A common capability API hides modem and regional differences. Products compose their own HMI and policy. One legacy product receives an adapter with a two-release migration deadline rather than a permanent fork.
commonMistakes: Maximizing shared code instead of shared product value
Forcing all products into the lowest-common-denominator UX
Adding extension points without ownership and compatibility rules
Measuring platform success by library or component count
